doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Vincent the clarinetist, the Larrick theatre and the elephant
summary: Tom recalls bringing a fine clarinetist named Vincent to New Orleans, and playing for shows at the Larrick theatre, including an elephant that would not go up on the stage.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I don't know Dad. That Vincent, his name is Vincent.

Yeah, Vincent, that's him. He was playing clarinet. I believe, uh, my Aunt Handley. Handley was playing clarinet. I kept him all around, because he was sitting in good clarinet. Yeah, that's what they say. He was a good clarinet. Yes, sir. And I say, you're too good to stay over here. That's why I brought him over here. And he used to play for the, what they say, in the, not the palace, that was broken. Larrick? Larrick.
Yeah. Used to go there and play the lights when that show come.
Yeah, your show used to come there at the Larrick stage, before they broke it down. You take, uh... And they had an old elephant there. What was the, uh, the, uh... He wouldn't get up on the stage.
He wouldn't get up on the stage. They had a retro...

What was it? Elephant? Elephant. Elephant. Had a big elephant in there. Animal act. And they wasn't going to show him. Yeah. On the stage. But they brought him in the pasture, in the park here. Yeah.
